answer: Minting accounts is cheap; seeding them is not. Each season, the beacon publishes coordinates over a stretch of sea, and every account that wants weight must return a signed photo proving one body physically stood there - an island, a lotus farm, a harbor on the horizon. Two accounts cannot occupy one spot at one moment, so a farm of clones needs farms of bodies, scattered and unhireable in bulk. Identity here is anchored outside the ledger entirely.
